page.title: Day 1 against Neave's manual
page.standfirst_html: Every flag the comparator raised for Day 1, adjudicated against D.Day.1.07Feb22.pdf — whose page images had to be generated first, since Day 1 was converted before that workflow existed and its PNGs had never been made. Two findings needed more than the extracted text. Printed p29's connecting prose is set in a substitution-encoded font that pdftotext returns as mojibake, so six correct paragraphs looked invented; I derived the cipher from a sentence of known plaintext, decoded the page, and confirmed the site matches it word for word. And the same font's space character surfaces elsewhere as a stray ! — noise in the extract, but twice it was transcribed onto the site as a literal character. The headline is a whole indented note missing from printed p32, on why Neave says “variation” rather than “variability”. Two page anchors also turned out to be named for the wrong page, which sends six cross-references from the appendix and Optional Extras to the wrong place.

items.chip: Anchor named for the wrong page; five cross-refs land two pages early
items.flag: Not flagged — found by checking every sec-pageN anchor against the source
items.source_html: Printed p4 opens with the section heading The British Deming Association and later. Printed p6 is a different place entirely — it carries the EST extract (“a remarkable statistical technique which, to all intents and purposes, was unknown at the time of the original edition”) and the small-print paragraph, both in 03-statistics.qmd.
items.site_html: ## The British Deming Association and later {#sec-page6} — the anchor sits on printed p4 but is named for p6. No sec-page4 exists, and printed p6 has no anchor at all.
items.evidence_html: Every sec-pageN in Day 1 was checked by locating its anchored text in the source: all but this one and D1-09 sit on the page they name. Five references across the appendix and Optional Extras say “Day 1 page 6” — appendix/01-day-1.qmd:11 and :15, optional-extras/00-introduction.qmd:94, 03-part-c-ne-er-twain.qmd:13, 05-part-e-normality.qmd:33 — and all five resolve here, to printed p4. Two of them name their target: “the small-print paragraph beginning at the bottom of Day 1 page 6” and “In extract from EST on Day 1 page 6” — both of which are on printed p6, in 03-statistics.qmd, not on p4. Renaming to sec-page4 also repairs 04-resources.qmd:123, whose “(see page 4)” currently reaches the right paragraph through a wrongly-named anchor. The five appendix links must move to the new sec-page6 in the same change, or they break.

sections.title: Emphasis
sections.note_html: Invisible to every automated flag — pdftotext discards italic, bold and colour.

items.chip: Deming's phrase starts a word late, and its italic is lost
items.flag: Not flagged — pdftotext discards colour and italics alike
items.source_html: • He was concerned not with mere change but with transformation of Western style of management (his own term for it).
items.site_html: * He was concerned not with mere change but with transformation of Western style of management (his own term for it).
items.proposal: * He was concerned not with mere change but with *transformation* of Western style of management (his own term for it).
items.evidence_html: On the page image the blue run begins at “transformation” and continues to “management”, with “transformation” alone in italic. The site starts the .deming_quote span three words later, so “transformation of” prints black and unemphasised. Worth a second look before accepting: .deming_quote is styled bold + italic in main.css:337, so widening the span italicises the whole phrase rather than just the one word the source emphasises — which is closer in colour but further in emphasis. Recorded here rather than under a fix because the trade-off is a judgement call, not a transcription error.

sections.title: Checked and cleared
sections.note_html: Comparator artifacts and documented site-wide conventions. Grouped by cause, because Day 1's volume is dominated by a few mechanical ones.

items.chip: Autolinked URLs are stripped to nothing before comparison
items.page: PDF p8, p15, p38 · printed p4, p11, p34
items.source_html: … the Deming Alliance … The Alliance’s website is <mark class='src'>www.demingalliance.org</mark> and their meetings are held in the Midlands.
items.site_html: … The Alliance’s website is <mark class='gone'>(nothing)</mark> and their meetings are held in the Midlands.
items.evidence_html: Not a site defect. Day 1 writes URLs as Markdown autolinks — <https://www.demingalliance.org> — and scripts/lib/qmd_strip.py has no autolink handling at all (grep for autolink returns nothing), so it removes them as if they were HTML tags. The URL is present and visible on the site in every one of these nine flags; the comparator simply cannot see it. Same shape as #784, and I have proposed raising it as its own issue rather than patching the scorer mid-pass — see the note under “Out of scope”.

items.chip: Connecting prose is set in a substitution-encoded font
items.source_html: *+)!,-.)/0!12!3$!-1/0!4,3)/!56,3!#2!120)62#-!3)3,!76100)2!8$!91--1#3!:60,2; … which decodes to “The oldest in my list comes from an internal memo written by William Orton, …”
items.site_html: The oldest in my list comes from an internal memo written by William Orton, President of Western Electric, the American communications company, in 1876:
items.evidence_html: Not a site defect, and checked rather than assumed. On printed p29 the quotations are in a normal font but every connecting sentence is in a subset font whose glyphs carry arbitrary codes, so pdftotext emits mojibake and the comparator finds no source for six correct paragraphs. I derived the substitution map from one sentence of known plaintext and decoded the whole page: all six paragraphs match the site word for word, including “Even Albert Einstein was not to be left out of my list.” and the Decca paragraph's two full stops. The page image confirms the italic on different in the closing paragraph is also correct.

items.chip: Cipher-font space renders as “!” inside ordinary sentences
items.page: PDF p7, p9, p13, p36, p38, p44 · printed p3, p5, p9, p32, p34, p40
items.source_html: That seemed reasonable enough to me, but what astonished me was the length of the seminar: four days. <mark class='src'>!</mark>Four days?
items.site_html: …the length of the seminar: four days. Four days?
items.evidence_html: Not a site defect. The same cipher-font space behind C-02 leaks into otherwise-normal lines as a stray !, usually just before an italic run or a colon introducing a quotation. In each of these seven the site's text is right and the source extract is what is damaged. Note the direction matters: where the artifact appears in the extract it is noise, but where it was copied onto the site it is a real defect — that is D1-04 and D1-05, and it is why this class was swept rather than waved through.

items.page: PDF p20, p23 · printed p16, p19

items.site_html: My commentary will be in the subsequent shaded red box. … writing some notes on the first few thoughts that come into your mind.
items.evidence_html: Not a site defect. A stray 0 from the page's decorative furniture lands mid-sentence in the extract; there is no digit at either point on the page. The reference-token check surfaces the first one as a bare-numeral mismatch, which is the check behaving correctly on bad input.

items.source_html: I we<mark class='src'>l</mark>I remember a time that I met up with an old acquaintance.
items.site_html: I well remember a time that I met up with an old acquaintance.
items.evidence_html: Not a site defect — the site's “well” is right and the extract's “welI” is an extraction misread. The same sentence recurs correctly at printed p36 (“I well remember the occasion …”), where the extractor gets it right.

items.chip: Contents and outline pages have no prose counterpart
items.source_html: Helpful books and videos (p 11) Activities, Major Activities, Pauses for Thought, Projects and “your organisation” (p 14) Outline of the course (p 16) … D DAY 1: THE “OVERTURE” and THE DEMING STORY
items.site_html: No counterpart — the site's navigation replaces the printed contents list, and the two flow diagrams are described in prose for screen readers rather than transcribed as scrambled table text.
items.evidence_html: Not site defects. These are the day's contents pages, the binder-tab cover, and two diagrams (“Organisation Viewed as a System”, the Chain Reaction) whose labels pdftotext reads as run-together prose — “Design and Consumer redesign research Suppliers of Consumers materials and equipment”. The site carries both diagrams with written descriptions, which is why Unsourced 1 and 5 also appear: that description text only ever existed on the site.

items.chip: Bullet run reads as missing because of the length floor
items.source_html: • It’s an environment that brings things together, rather than splitting them up e.g. into individual cost-centres, profit-centres, and the like.
items.site_html: * It’s an environment that brings things together, rather than splitting them up e.g. into individual cost-centres, profit-centres, and the like.
items.evidence_html: Not site defects. Both “missing” bullets are present and correct (09-different.qmd:37 and :64), and the eleven altered flags in this run are the comparator pairing each bullet against its neighbour — every bullet was read against the source page and matches. The one real difference found inside this run is the dropped full stop, raised separately as D1-10, and the emphasis question as D1-13.

items.chip: Quotation attributions split across the sentence boundary
items.page: PDF p12, p21, p27, p40, p42 · printed p8, p17, p23, p36, p38
items.source_html:
As Mrs Kilian later wrote on page 18 of her biography:
“American industrialists who watched the programme …”
items.site_html: … on page 18 of her biography: “American industrialists who watched the programme …” — one block on the site, two on the page.
items.evidence_html: Not site defects. Where the source runs an attribution line into an indented quotation, the site sets them as one paragraph plus a blockquote, so the sentence splitter pairs each half against the wrong counterpart and both score low. Each was read against its page: the wording is identical. “Quite some paradox.” (Altered 1) and “Four days?” (Unsourced 3) are the same effect seen from the other side — both are present, at 03-statistics.qmd:111 and 02-rediscovered.qmd:80.

items.chip: Site-only conventions: enrichment, workbook refs, archived links
items.page: PDF p8, p19, p40 · printed p4, p15, p36
items.source_html: … obtainable from the Learning Store at the Deming Transformation Forum in the UK (www.deming.org.uk) … | So (whether you are using a printed copy of the Workbook or of the com- plete material), if that discussion is visible …
items.site_html: … (www.deming.org.uk<mark class='src'>; site no longer online, 2012 archived snapshot linked</mark>) … | So, if that discussion is visible …
items.evidence_html: Not site defects, three established conventions. The archived-snapshot note is a deliberate editorial addition for a dead link, and it is what the reference check reports as a QMD-only “2012”. The Workbook parenthetical is omitted site-wide — the site has no printed workbook, the same reason [WB NN] markers are dropped throughout the corpus. And Out of the Crisis page 270[315] is the course's dual-edition citation style, not an inserted number.

items.source_html: b (page 2) Copyright© Deming Prize Committee. All Rights Reserved. http://www.juse.or.jp/deming_en/
items.site_html: [^a]: Copyright© Deming Prize Committee. All Rights Reserved. <https://www.juse.or.jp/deming_en/>
items.evidence_html: Not a site defect. “All Rights Reserved.” is short enough that its closest match anywhere in the PDF is an unrelated sentence, which is what put it in the unsourced list; the full line is present and correct as footnote b's text. The scheme is upgraded from http to https, in line with the other links on the day.

sections.title: Out of scope for this pass
sections.note_html: Real, but a per-day content pass is the wrong instrument.

items.chip: qmd_strip.py should render autolinks as their URL text
items.source_html: scripts/lib/qmd_strip.py strips <https://example.com> to nothing.
items.site_html: Pandoc renders an autolink as visible URL text, so the stripped QMD is missing text the reader can see — and every sentence containing a URL scores as altered.
items.proposal: Raise as an issue against #734, alongside #784.
items.evidence_html: A comparator bug rather than a site defect, and the same shape as #784: the stripper drops text Pandoc keeps, producing false “altered” flags against correct site text. Deliberately not fixed inside this pass — qmd_strip.py is one of the six files in SCORER_VERSION_FILES, so editing it restales all fifteen results/*.yml records and invalidates the report this adjudication is built against. It belongs in a window with no content pass open.
items.outcome: Raised as #793, alongside #784, for a scorer window with no content pass open.
